components.name: Room Card Material
components.description: Repeated content panel without individual backdrop blur.
components.html: <button class="ds-card">ห้องประชุม</button>
components.css: .ds-card{background:#fff;color:#222735;border:1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 85%);border-radius:16px;box-shadow:0 8px 28px rgb(37 48 75 / 7%),inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 90%);padding:18px 20px;font-family:inherit;cursor:pointer;transition:box-shadow 180ms ease-out,border-color 180ms ease-out}.ds-card:hover{border-color:rgb(164 35 59 / 30%);box-shadow:0 12px 32px rgb(37 48 75 / 12%),inset 0 1px 0 white}.ds-card:disabled{opacity:.72}@supports(backdrop-filter:blur(1px)){.ds-card{background:rgb(255 255 255 / 65%)}}@media(prefers-reduced-transparency:reduce){.ds-card{background:#fff}}@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-card{transition:none}}.ds-button:focus-visible,.ds-field:focus-visible,.ds-nav button:focus-visible,.ds-card:focus-visible{outline:3px solid #a4233b;outline-offset:3px}

narrative.overview: Apple-inspired translucent chrome sits over a soft lavender and blue neutral surface. Burgundy remains the action and selection accent, with Thai text and existing room-booking content preserved.
keyCharacteristics: Cool neutral surfaces with restrained burgundy emphasis.
Translucent chrome, readable controls, and softly rounded containers.
Responsive desktop frame and mobile dock.
Opaque material fallback and reduced transparency support.

rules.name: The Accent Rule
rules.body: Preserve burgundy for action and selection; keep shared chrome neutral.

rules.name: The Bounded Blur Rule
rules.body: Apply blur to chrome, dialogs, account options, the login control panel, and search controls; leave repeated content cards without individual backdrop blur.

dos: Do preserve Thai labels, burgundy identity, and existing booking layouts.
Do use the shared material tokens for recurring panels and chrome.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, opaque fallback, and reduced transparency behavior.
donts: Don't add individual backdrop blur to repeated room cards.
Don't use the glass treatment to replace semantic status colors or obscure text.
